institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I like the country and thought it could be interesting to try to live there for a period. Meanwhile it was one of the places where I could actually find some courses that fit my interests.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my stay abroad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most information was available online so I think it was okay easy to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction week for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was a bit stressful as a lot of students was looking for private accommodation. I used a little bit more than a month to find a place, and first found it to weeks before the stay started. So, first of all I will recommend starting look a little bit early if you want a place in good time. On the other hand, it was also possible to find something after arrival because a lot of Norwegians first put there room online just before the want to rent it out, so in that sense the opportunities became better the closer the stay came.
I found my room through
hybel.no
, and that is a nice site to use. A good idea is to make a profile about yourself and that you look for a room, then people can contact you, that worked for me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Very nice to live off campus as a danish student. I lived with norwegians which was very nice. Also I got the opportunity to life very central compared to the accomodations on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The univeristy did not secure nordic student with housing which is ok as we had a better change of finding private housing. There were many candidates but in the end my impression was that most people found a nice place.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy. Only proplem was that some courses you needed to write the department because you could not sign up yourself. So as long you know that it is possible to take courses that you cannot signed up to yourself it was fine.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The nice thing about NTNU is that you can sign up to too many courses and try some different out before you finally choose which one you take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Homepages and the study administration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful, I could sign up to the classes it wanted after I wrote an email to the department.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are in doubt just ask the study administration or the lectures they are helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Technological there where a bit behind KU. Some lectures where nice and others where not good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is lower than KU. I had a course of 15 ECTS but I thounght the workload was the same as a 7,5 ECTS at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style is very similar to KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SØK3522 - Labor Economics
SØK3007 - Skatt, beslutningsatferd og økonomisk politikk
INTRO175 - Introduction to Norway

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Labor economics was niced and was teached like courses at KU.
Skatt, beslutningsatferd og økonomisk politikk was not very good as it was only theory and no empirics and not very relevant for the real world as the lecture did not put any perspectives on the theory.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had bought bus and train tickets to travel green to the destination but few days before my departure Norway was hit by a heavy storm that created floods. This closed the railways and roads, so I needed to buy an expensive train ticket last minute to get to the destination in time.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
In general, Norway is said to be very expensive but Copenhagen is expensive to live in as well so it was not that bad compared to home. I actually used less money that I had expected. 
Some groceries are very expensive but others are cheaper so maybe you just change you habits a bit.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So cool and nice study enviroment in Trondheim. Almost all student vulenteers in some club or bar or studyboard. There is a lot of opportunities for sports and clubs for many different stuff. There happens a lot a nice stuff at Studentersamfundet.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Fitness opportunities that also gave you acces to try different sports clubs as badminton, dance, volley and so on. 
Every second autumn there is the festival UKA, that I got to experience which is arranged by student volunteers.
There is a lot of conserts and other stuff at Studentersamfundet through the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you like sports I would recommend a 6-month mebership to SIT and NTNUI. This also give the opportunity to get on trips with the outdoor-club. 
I would off course also reccomend Studentersamfundet.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the nature in Trondheim but also go on trips to Trollheimen, Dovre and other mountain areas that is around 2 hours from Trondheim. These areas have the great mountain nature of Norway. So many beutiful places to visit but also nice just to enjoy Trondheim there is a lot to see and opportunities to enjoy nature as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy as it is so close to the danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live with them and you can also sign up student clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any I think.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language I guess.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open minded and enjoy it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of danish exchange student going to the distination from different universities then I was there in the autumn.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be abroad and a away from everything and one yoy know and act in that situation. Also to get a little break and enjoy the nature and have time for other things than what you have in the weekday at home. And to meet new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The examination period.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I was in a lot of doubt if I should go, but now I am just so greateful that I did it and have the feeling that there was no reason to be in doubt because it was sush a nive experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
